content: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by bacteria that spread through the air and can infect anyone. In some cases, individuals may become infected with TB bacteria but do not immediately develop the disease. In such situations, the bacteria remain inactive in the body, and the individual is considered to have a TB infection. People with TB infection do not exhibit any symptoms or signs of the disease. It is estimated that approximately one in four people worldwide have a TB infection, most of whom remain healthy. However, some individuals with TB infection may progress to develop active TB disease, particularly if their immune system becomes weakened. To determine if you have a TB infection, diagnostic tests such as the tuberculin skin test (TST) or interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) can be used. These tests help identify individuals who may benefit from preventive treatment. Preventive treatment for TB is essential to stop the infection from progressing to active disease. Today, there are several effective preventive treatment options available. By adhering to the prescribed treatment regimen, the risk of developing active TB disease can be significantly reduced.
